purpose: Natural descriptions of AI systems, written the way a business user talks to an assistant, for measuring the front door of euaiact_classify_system end to end. 228 describe a regulated system. 106 must never come back high-risk or prohibited: 60 hard negatives that share vocabulary with a regulated category, and 46 systems that sit inside a regulated sector without performing a listed use.
caveats: Synthetic. Written by three language models on 2026-09-19 under one brief that forbade the regulation's own terms of art and asked for the decisive facts to be stated.

The labels of the 228 regulated descriptions are the writing model's and were not verified one by one; some, notably under annex_iii_1, are arguable. Aggregate recognition over them is a metric, never a legal assertion about a single description.

The 106 negatives were reviewed by hand. Of the 46 in-sector ones, 24 were written by hand against the Annex wording and 22 by a model that never saw the tool definition. None may come back high-risk or prohibited.

Known wrong labels, left in place so that recordings stay comparable: s2-annex_iii_7-05 describes the verification of travel documents, which Annex III(7)(d) expressly excepts; s3-annex_iii_8-04 describes campaign analytics that voters are never exposed to, which Annex III(8)(b) excludes; s2-annex_iii_7-01 describes one-to-one verification of a traveller against a passport and is arguable. An agent that declines to call these high-risk is right, and the score counts it as a miss.
